notes:
**A dead email address at a domain you do not own is not yours to fix.** Docket
found three example addresses in a forum's how-to about configuring mailboxes,
checked the domain, correctly established that mail to it bounces — and then
told the site to add DNS records for a domain belonging to someone else.

The check already limited itself to real `mailto:` links, on the reasoning that
an address written in prose might only be an example. Forum and documentation
software auto-links bare addresses, so the examples arrive looking exactly like
real ones.

Docket cannot tell a documentation example from a genuine contact address. It
can tell whose domain it is, and that is enough to stop recommending a repair
the reader has no way to make. The finding still appears — a dead address on
your page is worth knowing about whoever owns the domain — but the advice now
says the domain is not yours, and that if it is an example, nothing needs doing.
